name: M 5.7 - 47 km WNW of Khuzdar, Pakistan

kindsOfChange.bothFell: both channels fell: typical of open water, or of ground made smooth
kindsOfChange.bothRose: both channels rose: typical of wetter or rougher ground
kindsOfChange.hhRose: HH rose alone: typical of water standing under plants
kindsOfChange.hhFell: HH fell alone: typical of a smoother or drier surface
kindsOfChange.hvRose: HV rose alone: typical of growing plants (more leaves and branches)
kindsOfChange.hvFell: HV fell alone: typical of lost leaves and branches (a burn, a harvest, a clearing)
kindsOfChange.other: the channels moved against each other

rough.two: Only two passes lie before the event, so the second key, the cell's own longer history, is missing. In our test about three in four cells flagged this way on quiet ground are right.
rough.pair: Only one pass lies before the event: there is no past to learn what is ordinary from. The step between the two passes is set against its own spread over the area, and the threshold is the one theory gives. In our test about one cell in four flagged this way is right.

summary: On NISAR's first pass after the event of 2026-10-17 (2026-10-22), 6.4 % of the cells stood out from what they had read on the 4 passes before it. On those passes themselves the same rules flag 0.1 %.
method: NISAR L2 GCOV backscatter in cells of 500 m. From each pass the middle of all cells is taken away, so that what moved the whole area alike drops out. Each cell is then set against its own usual value and spread over the passes before (at an event: before the event; at least 3, at most 10), in HH and, where recorded, HV. The threshold is the score that 1% of the cells exceeded when each baseline pass was judged against the others. A cell counts only if at least 2 of its eight neighbours are over the threshold too.
limits: It says that the ground changed and where, not why. A baseline of a few passes knows nothing of the season: a crop growing or ground freezing stands out as well. Cells next to each other share speckle and weather, so a cluster is weaker evidence than its size suggests.
